subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename bootstrap files as a core hook contract, or keep `bootstrap-extra-files` limited to recognized workspace bootstrap filenames?
rationale: The implementation path is mechanically bounded, but it changes startup context and configured workspace-file loading scope, which is a product and security-boundary decision rather than a strict bug repair.

options.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
options.body: Allow explicitly configured custom-basename files through the existing hook path once the linked PR or replacement is rebased and preserves guards, budgets, docs, and tests.

options.title: Keep Recognized Basenames Only
options.body: Reject arbitrary workspace-file injection and route custom context requests to narrower first-class filename or workspace-convention proposals.

options.title: Defer To Broader Context API
options.body: Pause this request until maintainers choose a broader workspace discovery or context-file API instead of expanding the existing hook contract.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
recommendation.body: Allow explicitly configured custom-basename files through the existing hook path once the linked PR or replacement is rebased and preserves guards, budgets, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original hook feature and has recent ownership signals in the workspace bootstrap loader path.
